previous_assumption: assumed LogsheetService.submitLogsheet needed no validation beyond org ownership of the rental, and that seed-demo-data.ts's daysFromNow-based Journey 1 execution timeline was immune to new server-layer date rules the way it was immune to the earlier Zod-contract-only date validation pass
correction: submitLogsheet had zero checks: no rental-status gate (a still-confirmed, never-mobilized rental could get logsheets) and no date bounds (any logDate accepted regardless of the rental's own start/end, or whether it was in the future). Fixed both, service-layer this time, not Zod -- the active-status rule needs the Rental record in hand, not just the request body. That distinction matters: seed-demo-data.ts bypasses every Zod contract by calling services directly, which is why it survived every earlier date-validation pass unscathed, but service-layer checks apply to it just the same as any real caller. Its Journey 1 timeline used daysFromNow offsets landing in the future for mobilization/logsheets/invoice/payment, which the new future-logDate check correctly rejected -- fixed by shifting that whole cascade back 15 days so it represents a rental that already started and has been running, which is also a more realistic demo than a not-yet-started rental with logsheets already against it. Also fixed the same screenshot's 'Rental days: -10' -- daysBetweenInclusive(start, end ?? today) goes negative for a future-start open-ended rental, clamped to floor 0. Lesson: before adding a new validation rule in a SERVICE method (as opposed to a Zod contract), check seed-demo-data.ts's calls to that exact service method specifically -- the earlier assumption that the seed script is categorically immune to date rules only holds for contract-level rules, not service-level ones.
